text:
maya: Heads-up — between 12:05 and 12:20 we started seeing a sudden wave of connection resets from gpt-serving in eastus1 GPU pool. Pods reporting 'connection reset by peer' and grpc errors. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/abcd/conntrack?var-region=eastus1 :grimacing:

raj: Checking infra metrics now. conntrack entries jumped from ~42k to ~98k in ~10m. nf_conntrack_max = 100000. We're dangerously close to ceiling.

natalie: That would definitely cause SNAT failures if table saturates. Are we seeing many short-lived client connections?

liam: Quick probe on an affected node: `sudo conntrack -S` -> tcp: 98641, udp: 1213. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` -> 100000. ip_local_port_range = 32768 61000 (only ~28233 ports). Pattern is many ephemeral ports + short TTL.

maya: Traffic pattern fits: prefetch / warmup workers from router creating 1–3s connections, no keepalive. Prefetch burst at ~11:58 caused peak.

raj: Immediate mitigation options (ranked low->high risk):
- scale down prefetchers / throttle spikes (app change)
- enable HTTP keep-alive on client side (reduce new TCP handshakes)
- increase nf_conntrack_max temporarily
- widen ip_local_port_range / change SNAT strategy (nodePort vs clusterIP)
- add per-node SNAT pools / eBPF passthrough (longer-term)

natalie: For now please do two things: (1) throttle prefetchers to stop bursts, (2) apply a small sysctl bump on affected nodes to prevent immediate saturation.

liam: Applying quick change on two busiest nodes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 61000'`. Also set `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` to recycle TIME_WAIT quicker. Watching for side-effects.

maya: Deploy-bot — triggered patch to throttle prefetchers (patch/keepalive-prefetch@maya).

deploy-bot: Deployment started: patch/keepalive-prefetch@maya — rolling update 2/6 nodes.

raj: After sysctl bump and throttle we see conntrack count drop to ~65k over 8m. No new 502s reported. Still watching.

natalie: Next steps (follow-up):
- make nf_conntrack_max bump part of k8s node daemonset with a guard (but don't set too high without testing)
- add conntrack usage alert: alert if > 70% nf_conntrack_max for >5m
- implement app-level keepalive / connection pooling for prefetch clients
- evaluate node-local SNAT or eBPF to avoid global conntrack pressure

raj: Filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-7890 — 'eastus1 port-thundering: conntrack exhaustion & SNAT mitigation' with logs/graphs attached.

maya: Thanks everyone. Good quick teamwork. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident resolved? set to MONITORING — created incident INC-2026 and assigned to eng-infra.

liam: Will schedule a pressure test to validate daemonset changes and port-range impacts (noisy test during maintenance window).

natalie: Also add a small doc snippet to run quick checks: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count`, `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`, `conntrack -S`, `ss -s` — handy for on-call.

maya: Filed PR for runbook additions at https://git.redwood.net/infra/runbooks/-/merge_requests/123

raj: Locking this thread. Monitor for the rest of the day and escalate if counts rebound.
